body.en: Movement stands at the center of Tidal Rhythms. As a way to reconnect, to our bodies, our emotions, our identities and ancestries, to one another, and to the world around us.

quote.en: When we meet our difficult experiences with care and tenderness — or with rawness and surrender — we come back to ourselves.

pillarSomaticBody.en: We begin with body awareness: sensing, breathing, moving, and listening to what is present. Somatic awareness offers another way of knowing ourselves — one that can unfold beyond words and through sensation, movement, and pleasure.

pillarRelationalBody.en: Healing happens in relationship. You are accompanied in this therapeutic space where your experience can be expressed, explored, and met with curiosity and compassion. Through movement, words, writing, and conversation, we create new possibilities for relating to yourself and others.

pillarAgencyBody.en: We explore your capacity to sense, choose, express, and act. Dance creates a space to experience agency in the body — to discover that you can move, change direction, take space, set boundaries, connect, and create.

pillarContextualBody.en: We are shaped by the worlds we belong to. Personal experiences are connected to family histories, culture, society, and our environment. When relevant, we make space for collective and transgenerational experiences of trauma, displacement, oppression, or loss, without reducing your story to them.

pillarSlowBody.en: Sessions are 60 minutes, held in a studio in the 11th arrondissement in Paris. It can take place weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly, according to your needs and rhythm.

sessionIntro.en: You do not need any formal dance training. We cultivate your body's own natural expression.

sessionArriveBody.en: A gentle grounding practice to help you land in the present moment and tune into your body.

sessionExploreBody.en: Space to speak about what is present for you, your needs, and your expectations. From there, we move into guided exercises, improvisation, or simply noticing what your body is communicating.

sessionIntegrateBody.en: We close through words, drawing, or writing — reflecting on what emerged so you can carry that wisdom beyond the session.

blurb.en: A slow process for deeper healing.

p1.en: My work is centered on creating shared moments where we can be present, sensitive, creative together; where we can reflect on the cultures we are part of and our ways of seeing.

p2.en: The co-created workshops are primarily based on movement, collective dialogue, and musical soundscapes to reflect on a variety of connected topics such as patriarchy, mental health, and ecology. I have also offered dance as therapy, for domestic violence and sexual violence survivors in an institutional framework.

p3.en: Dance, movement, is an integral part of the workshops. I see movement as a way to reconnect to our body, to the persons that surround us, to the life that surrounds us, and to the nature we may not always see, but can feel.

p4.en: Personally, dancing is a practice of decolonization. Of Vietnamese and U.S. origins, I feel the legacy of colonialism, racism, and war. Through dance, I find the space to embody, and release.

trainingsList.en:
• Master's in Dance Movement Therapy Université Paris Cité, Institute of Psychology, 2024–2026
    • Research Thesis: "Reconstructing the Self: How Dance Movement Therapy Contributes to the Resilience Process of Displaced Persons with Complex Trauma"
    • Professional Thesis: "The Place of Culture in Care: Dance Movement Therapy with Bicultural Children in a CMPP"
    • 550 hours of clinical internship experience with children, adults, women, and displaced persons in hospitals, associations, and a multidisciplinary mental health clinic across the Paris region, France.
  • Authentic flow 200H training Portugal, July 2023
  • Body-Mind-Centering (BMC) 144H training with Tamara Milla Vigo France, 2022
  • "Fundamentals in Dance-movement therapy", 32H training with Benoit Lesage France, February 2021
  • Dance-rhythm therapy 50H training with France Schott-Billmann France, October 2021
  • Masters in Interdisciplinary approaches to research and education - Learning Sciences - Center for Interdisciplinary research (now Learning Planet Institute), Université de Paris France, 2019-2021
    • Masters thesis: "Examining trauma-informed care: University students’ mental health experiences and strategies of mental health care during the COVID-19 pandemic"
    • Thesis presented at two conferences:

      "Colloque du Care", Montpellier, France, November 2021

      "Colloque Numérique et pandémie. Les enjeux d’éthique un an après", online, July 2021

    • Research project and workshop creation: what is collective trauma, and can we heal it through somatic therapies?
  • Contemporary dance practice since childhood, improvisation for +7 years
